name: Ibuprofen
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Ibuprofen is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) eliminated in urine as inactive metabolites. NSAIDs reduce kidney blood flow and can cause acute kidney injury, especially with diuretics, ACE inhibitors, heart failure, liver disease, older age or existing kidney impairment. The US prescription label does not recommend ibuprofen in advanced renal disease.
kidney_function_basis: Label uses 'impaired renal function' and 'advanced renal disease' without a CrCl number. Mapping 'advanced' to CrCl <30 is our judgment.

bands.recommendation: Usual: pain 400 mg every 4 to 6 hours as needed; arthritis 1,200 to 3,200 mg/day in 3 or 4 doses; maximum 3,200 mg/day (label). Lowest effective dose, shortest duration.

No label dose change. Impaired kidney function is a risk factor for NSAID kidney injury: monitor creatinine, potassium and blood pressure; avoid volume depletion and the ACE inhibitor or ARB plus diuretic combination.
bands.short: No dose change; monitor SCr, K, BP

bands.recommendation: Not recommended in advanced renal disease (no controlled data); if it must be started, monitor kidney function closely (label, Warnings: Advanced Renal Disease).
Not recommended in advanced renal disease (no controlled data); if it must be started, monitor kidney function closely (label, Warnings: Advanced Renal Disease).

hd.text: Not recommended (advanced renal disease; label). NSAIDs may hasten loss of residual kidney function.

pd.text: Not recommended (advanced renal disease; label). NSAIDs may hasten loss of residual kidney function.

crrt.text: Avoid: NSAIDs can worsen acute kidney injury.

monitoring: Creatinine, potassium and blood pressure in CKD, heart failure, liver disease, older adults, or with diuretics, ACE inhibitors or ARBs. Gastrointestinal bleeding; hemoglobin with long-term use.

pediatric.approved_ages: The selected prescription tablet label is not for children; PH registers ibuprofen oral suspensions and drops used for fever and pain in children (separate OTC labeling, not stored).
pediatric.usual_dose: Not given in this label (pediatric suspensions are OTC products with separate labeling).

renal.recommendation: No kidney dose change; keep the child hydrated. NSAID-associated acute kidney injury occurs in children, mostly after correctly dosed NSAIDs and with dehydration; children under 5 had more severe AKI (Misurac 2013). Avoid during vomiting, diarrhea or poor intake.
